newsitem.title: CANADA: TCPL says is behind in Sable gas pipe race.
newsitem.headline: TCPL says is behind in Sable gas pipe race.

text.p: TransCanada PipeLines Ltd chief executive George Watson conceded on Thursday that his firm was behind in the race to build a pipeline from the Sable Island natural gas project off Canada's east coast.

But TransCanada, which is in partnership with Gaz Metropolitain & Co LP in its bid to move gas from the planned offshore Nova Scotia project, is far from writing off its proposal, Watson told reporters after TransCanada's anuual meeting.
"We're not throwing in the towel," Watson said. "We know we're late into this."

He said the Trans Quebec & Maritimes proposal was delayed by negotiations in Quebec, where TransCanada had to convince regulators and Gaz Metropolitain that a tolling structure that would have made it cheaper for east coast gas to move on the TCPL system than western Canadian gas was unfair.
Under the current system, the cost of expansion is rolled in to all shipper tolls for gas that flows from western to eastern Canada.
"Certain powers that be in Quebec including our partner were insisting that that should be rolled in all the way to Sable Island which would have given a far different cost increase," Watson said.
"We said that when there are two basins competing, it's commodity on commodity competition, not biased by the underlying costs of delivery."
The proposal would move Sable gas to New England from Nova Scotia New Brunswick and Quebec.
The C$1 billion project is in competition with the proposed Maritimes & Northeast pipeline which would also move the gas to New England but bypass Quebec and Canada's current pipeline network.
Maritimes & Northeast partners include Westcoast Energy Inc, PanEnergy Corp and Mobil Corp unit Mobil Oil Canada.
TransCanada officials said, however, that the U.S. leg of the company's proposal -- the Portland Natural Gas Transmission -- was ahead of the competition.
The 178 million cubic feet per day Portland pipeline is awaiting final U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission environmental approval. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
